entries.headline: Nasdaq futures jump 1.4% as chipmakers rebound from a $3 trillion rout
entries.dek: Nvidia, AMD and Micron rose in premarket trading a day after a rout tied to AI-regulation fears from Democrats' midterm win wiped nearly $3 trillion off the S&P 500.
entries.caption: Futures pointed higher Friday after chipmakers and AI infrastructure names stabilized from Thursday's steep market-wide selloff.

sources.title: Premarket: Nasdaq futures rise after steep AI selloff as chip stocks stabilize

brief: Nasdaq 100 E-minis rose 378.5 points, or 1.41%, by 6:24 a.m. ET Friday, while S&P 500 E-minis added 21.75 points, or 0.29%, and Dow E-minis fell 471 points, or 0.91%, Reuters reported. The moves followed Thursday's rout, in which the Nasdaq Composite posted its steepest one-day decline in 19 months and erased nearly $3 trillion from S&P 500 market value.

The rout followed Democrats' midterm election victory, including wins in several data-center states, which stoked fears that tougher AI regulation could slow data-center construction, Reuters reported. Jane Gibbons, an equity strategist at Jefferies, called the selloff 'reactionary, not a fundamental reset, driven by a collision of concerns around AI spend, policy and inflation.'

Nvidia rose 4.5% in premarket trading after its worst day since January 2025, and AMD, Intel, Broadcom and Micron Technology gained between 4.6% and 8.2%, Reuters reported. Traders were awaiting Friday's October jobs report, pricing in more than a 65% chance of a December rate increase, while Atlassian fell 14.1% and Airbnb rose 12.2% on earnings.
body: Nasdaq 100 E-minis rose 378.5 points, or 1.41%, by 6:24 a.m. ET Friday, while S&P 500 E-minis added 21.75 points, or 0.29%, and Dow E-minis fell 471 points, or 0.91%, Reuters reported. The rally followed Thursday's rout, in which the Nasdaq Composite posted its steepest one-day decline in 19 months, confirmed it had entered correction territory, and was headed for a fourth straight weekly fall. The CBOE Volatility Index, which logged its biggest one-day jump in about 19 months on Thursday, eased to 26.70 on Friday.

The selloff followed Democrats' midterm election victory, including wins in several key data-center states, which stoked fears that tougher AI regulation under a Democratic Congress could slow the buildout of AI data centers, Reuters reported. Jane Gibbons, an equity strategist at Jefferies, called Thursday's selloff 'reactionary, not a fundamental reset, driven by a collision of concerns around AI spend, policy and inflation.' Optimism over the sector's rapid growth had earlier propelled stock markets to record highs this year.

Nvidia added 4.5% in premarket trading after suffering its worst day since January 2025, when the emergence of the low-cost Chinese AI model DeepSeek had rattled Wall Street, Reuters reported. Other chip stocks, including AMD, Intel, Broadcom and Micron Technology, rose between 4.6% and 8.2% in premarket trading, following steep losses in the previous session.

Data-center operators IREN and Applied Digital, so-called neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius Group, and AI-exposed utilities and equipment suppliers such as GE Vernova and Constellation Energy all recovered from deep losses in the previous session, Reuters reported. The rebound came after those names had dropped sharply alongside chipmakers in Thursday's broader tech-led rout.

Elon Musk-led Tesla and SpaceX were also higher in premarket trading, up 2% and 4% respectively, after both had dropped sharply over the two previous sessions, Reuters reported. Megacap and growth stocks were broadly mixed Friday, the report said, even as chip and AI-infrastructure names that had fallen sharply a day earlier moved back up together in early trading.

A jump in crude oil prices on Thursday had also pressured equities, Reuters reported, on concerns that higher energy costs could feed inflation and push global central banks toward higher interest rates. Brent crude futures were broadly flat on Friday, but oil was still on track for sharp weekly declines, with the S&P 500 energy index on pace for a weekly drop of more than 11%. The S&P 500 overall was on course for its worst weekly performance since March 2025, when tariff policy had roiled global markets.

Investors were awaiting the October jobs report, due at 8:30 a.m. ET, for clues on the path of interest rates, with traders pricing in more than a 65% chance of a December rate increase, according to the CME FedWatch Tool cited by Reuters. Among individual movers, software firm Atlassian fell 14.1% after its first-quarter results, while Airbnb climbed 12.2% after the vacation-rental platform raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth forecast.

entries.headline: Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX have shed $456 billion since the midterms
entries.dek: Shares of both companies fell sharply this week as Democrats won control of Congress and unseated Musk allies in Texas, trimming his fortune by about $90 billion.
entries.caption: Markets digested a week of political upheaval as investors weighed new regulatory risk for major technology ventures.

sources.title: Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX lose over $420 billion in combined market cap after midterms

unverified_claims: Musk's net worth figures (over $1 trillion after SpaceX's IPO, now below $800 billion, a roughly $90 billion decline in the past week) are wealth estimates reported by CNBC rather than independently verified figures.
The claim that most of the candidates Musk backed lost their races rests on CNBC's own characterization rather than a specific vote tally given in the article.
brief: Tesla shares fell about 11% and SpaceX shares fell about 9% on Thursday afternoon, CNBC reported, pushing the two companies' combined market-cap losses past $420 billion since Tuesday's close. By the end of Thursday's session, CNBC said the combined loss had grown to about $456 billion.

CNBC attributed the selloff to investor reaction to the midterm election results, in which Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress. In Texas, where both companies are headquartered, Democratic candidates defeated longtime Musk allies, including gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa, who defeated incumbent Governor Greg Abbott, the report said.

body: Tesla shares fell about 11% and SpaceX shares fell about 9% on Thursday afternoon, CNBC reported, extending a slide that began after Tuesday's midterm election results were released. The declines pushed the two companies' combined market-capitalization losses past $420 billion since Tuesday's close, and by the end of Thursday's session CNBC said the combined loss had grown to about $456 billion.

CNBC attributed the selloff to investor reaction to the midterm election results, in which Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress. In Texas, where both Tesla and SpaceX are headquartered, Democratic candidates defeated longtime allies of Elon Musk, including gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa, who defeated incumbent Governor Greg Abbott, according to the report.

The report cited several specific investor concerns: the possibility of congressional probes into Musk and his companies, stricter regulatory oversight of artificial-intelligence infrastructure and data centers, potential delays to SpaceX's compute-capacity buildout in Texas, scrutiny of SpaceX's Starlink restrictions in Ukraine, and regulatory obstacles to a potential merger between Tesla and SpaceX.

The decline also affected Musk's personal fortune, which CNBC said had topped $1 trillion following SpaceX's initial public offering in June and has since fallen below $800 billion, a drop of roughly $90 billion over the past week, though CNBC noted he remains the world's richest person. Musk had contributed more than $470 million to Republican candidates and causes during the midterm campaign, and CNBC reported that most of the candidates he backed lost their races.

CM Bulletin tracks a space theme on the TSX Venture Exchange and the CSE each day, matching an issuer's registered name or sector label against the stories driving large-cap markets. On today's venture boards, no name assigned to the space theme traded enough volume to clear this bulletin's C$25,000 day-volume floor, the threshold used before any security is named in a read-through.

As a result, no venture issuer is named here in connection with today's Tesla and SpaceX story, and there is no group move to report for the space theme against the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. A stale price on a thinly traded name is not a reportable move, and the absence of qualifying trading today means the theme's venture names simply did not trade on it.

brief: IREN Limited said Thursday that more than $4 billion of contracted annualized revenue, expected by the end of 2026, will now arrive in January and potentially February. The company said the shift followed "a customer-requested change and supplier timing"; on the earnings call, co-CEO Daniel Roberts identified the customer as Microsoft, CNBC reported.

body: IREN Limited — described by CNBC as a "neocloud" — said Thursday that more than $4 billion of contracted annualized recurring revenue it had expected to reach by the end of 2026 will now arrive in January, and potentially as late as February. The company said the shift followed "a customer-requested change and supplier timing." On the earnings call, co-CEO Daniel Roberts identified the customer making the request as Microsoft, CNBC reported.

Roberts told CNBC that Microsoft had asked IREN to "reconfigure and upgrade some of the network infrastructure," and that the purpose was to let 200 megawatts of capacity serve "these latest-generation frontier models." Despite the later timing, the company said the more-than-$4-billion target remains "fully contracted and funded." IREN's shares rose in extended trading immediately after the results were released, CNBC reported, even after weeks of declines.

The report followed a rough stretch across AI infrastructure stocks: IREN's own shares had fallen 26% after Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections and were down 55% over the past month, CNBC reported, as the Nasdaq suffered its worst trading day since April 2025. Two other AI-infrastructure companies have fared similarly: CoreWeave has dropped 60% over the past month, and Nebius has declined 48% over the same period, both ahead of their own earnings reports this week.

Roberts told CNBC that "capital markets have become more selective in the last few weeks," adding that the market's questions had moved from "how big the contract is to whether it can be delivered, financed, and run at a profit." He said "there is a disconnect between what we're seeing in public market and what we're seeing at the customer level." IREN holds contracts with Nvidia, Microsoft and 13 other customers, CNBC reported.

Quarterly revenue rose 66% sequentially to $228 million, beating the $221 million average analyst estimate compiled by LSEG, CNBC reported. AI Cloud revenue more than doubled to $200 million, while IREN's net loss narrowed to $263 million from $684 million in the prior quarter. The company's bitcoin mining business, its original line of business before the shift to AI, supplied the remainder of quarterly revenue.

Revenue backlog grew 22% to $20.3 billion, with roughly two-thirds of it held by investment-grade counterparties, the company said. IREN also said it plans $15 billion of capital expenditure over the rest of its fiscal year, with $9 billion already covered by cash and committed financing and a further $6 billion in "target" financing "subject to market conditions." One customer has agreed to finance 90% of the GPU capital expenditure, Roberts said, and roughly a third of planned data-centre construction is being funded through customer prepayments for capacity.

On the venture boards, the read-through runs through the theme of artificial intelligence and data centres, which comprises 29 listed venture names. Eighteen of them traded today, none higher and 14 lower, for a median move of -7.11% against -0.99% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. AI-ML Innovations Inc. (CSE: AIML) fell 11.11% to C$0.04, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "ai." Railtown AI Technologies Inc (CSE: RAIL) fell 7.14% to C$0.26, also because its registered name contains "ai."

Three more names in the theme also fell: Rocket Doctor AI Inc. (CSE: AIDR) dropped 7.07% to C$0.46, also because its registered name contains "ai"; Edge Total Intelligence Inc (TSXV: CTRL) fell 6.00% to C$0.235, because its sector label is Software-Infrastructure; and Sparc AI Inc. (CSE: SPAI) fell 3.05% to C$1.91, again because its registered name contains "ai." The moves fell on the same day as IREN's results; nothing in today's trading connects the two.

entries.headline: Gold climbs to $4,063 an ounce as Democrats sweep control of Congress
entries.dek: Spot silver also rose to $52.32 an ounce and the US Dollar Index slipped to near 101.5 after Democrats won both the House and the Senate in the midterms.
entries.caption: Gold bars sit in secure storage, a traditional hedge for investors navigating currency and political uncertainty.

unverified_claims: The analyst commentary linking the gold and silver price moves to US dollar weakness, higher expected government spending and potential Federal Reserve quantitative easing reflects the stated opinions of Rich Checkan, Peter Schiff and Craig Hemke as quoted in the source; it is not independently verified market analysis.
brief: Spot gold climbed above US$4,000 an ounce on November 4, reaching US$4,063, while spot silver rose to US$52.32 by late afternoon. The move came as Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate in the US midterm elections, leaving President Trump facing an opposition Congress for the rest of his term.

The US Dollar Index fell about 0.3% to near 101.5 and Treasury yields moved lower. Analysts quoted in the report, including Peter Schiff of Euro Pacific Asset Management and Rich Checkan of Asset Strategies International, linked the moves to dollar weakness and expectations of higher government spending under a Democratic Congress.

The theme comprises 527 listed venture names; 349 traded today, 50 higher and 202 lower, for a median move of -2.20% against -0.99% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. Pantera Silver Corp (TSXV: PNTR) fell 24.24% to CAD0.25, and Aurania Resources Ltd (TSXV: ARU) rose 23.26% to CAD0.265.
body: Spot gold rose above US$4,000 an ounce on Wednesday, November 4, advancing to US$4,063, while spot silver climbed to US$52.32 by 4:55 p.m. EST. The US Dollar Index fell about 0.3% on the day, trading near 101.5, and Treasury yields moved lower. The moves came as vote counts from the US midterm elections showed Democrats taking control of both chambers of Congress.

The result leaves President Donald Trump facing a Congress controlled by the opposing party for the remainder of his term. Rich Checkan, president and chief operating officer of Asset Strategies International, speaking at the New Orleans Investment Conference ahead of the vote, said: "When it comes to precious metals, unless we are voting in a majority of politicians in this midterm who are then going to cut spending … unless that happens, gold is going higher."

Peter Schiff, chief economist and global strategist at Euro Pacific Asset Management, said a "Democrat takeover of Congress could be bullish for gold and silver," adding that the Federal Reserve could eventually turn to quantitative easing to contain rising bond yields. Craig Hemke, publisher of TFMetalsReport.com, said: "You can see where a big Democrat shift could be coming. But then to try to figure out the knockoff reactions of all these different markets, it's impossible to say."

The report does not characterize Wednesday's level as a record for either metal, and it draws no comparison with prices earlier in the week or the month. It also names no company or ticker tied to the gold or silver price move itself, beyond the three advisory firms whose principals were quoted on the midterm result.

On the venture boards, the gold and silver theme comprises 527 listed venture names; 349 traded today, 50 higher and 202 lower, for a median move of -2.20% against -0.99% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. Pantera Silver Corp (TSXV: PNTR) fell 24.24% to CAD0.25, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "silver." Aurania Resources Ltd (TSXV: ARU) rose 23.26% to CAD0.265, and is in the theme because its sector label is "Other Precious Metals & Mining."

Terra Rossa Gold Ltd (TSXV: TRR) rose 17.65% to CAD0.30, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "gold." Lighthouse Gold Inc. (CSE: LGHT) fell 16.67% to CAD0.05, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "gold." Slam Exploration Inc (TSXV: SXL) fell 16.67% to CAD0.05, and is in the theme because its sector label is "Gold." The moves and the midterm-linked gold and silver rally fell on the same trading day; nothing in the data connects them.
